mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: certified true copy issued by Companies Office, then apostille by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT). For any non-Apostille Convention state, use the parallel Consular Legalization path: Companies Office certified true copy, MFAT authentication, then legalization by that state's embassy or consulate accredited in New Zealand; the Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization paths are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: original Certificate of Good Standing from Companies Office, then apostille by New Zealand MFAT. For a non-Apostille Convention state, apply the parallel Consular Legalization path: original certificate, MFAT authentication, then consular legalization at the receiving state's mission in Wellington; never use apostille and consular legalization in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the proposed New Zealand Limited Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution by all directors before a New Zealand notary public; then Hague Apostille path: notary-certified copy, apostille by New Zealand MFAT. For a non-Apostille Convention state, use the parallel Consular Legalization path: notarization, MFAT authentication, then consular legalization by the receiving state's embassy or consulate in Wellington; both paths are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Subscriber shareholders and directors of the New Zealand Limited Company, adopted under Companies Act 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed original Articles of Association certified by a New Zealand notary public; then Hague Apostille path: notary-certified copy, apostille by New Zealand MFAT. For a non-Apostille Convention state, use the parallel Consular Legalization path: notarization, MFAT authentication, then consular legalization by the receiving state's embassy or consulate in Wellington; no document ever receives both an Apostille and a Consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Approved New Zealand registered bank (for example ANZ Bank New Zealand Limited, ASB Bank Limited, Bank of New Zealand, or Westpac New Zealand Limited) acting as an AML/CFT reporting entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letter from the bank's manager or compliance officer, certified by a New Zealand notary public; then Hague Apostille path: notary-certified copy, apostille by New Zealand MFAT. For a non-Apostille Convention state, use the Consular Legalization path only: notarization, MFAT authentication, then consular legalization by the receiving state's embassy or consulate in Wellington; apostille and consular legalization are not additive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The reporting entity must perform standard and enhanced customer due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2009 on all directors, shareholders, signatories and UBOs. Mandatory screening includes the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, New Zealand consolidated sanctions and export controls under the United Nations Sanctions Act 2020, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the Office of Foreign Assets Control 50-percent list, and any domestic NZ Watchlist circulated by the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit. All identified politically exposed persons - foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international organization PEPs as defined in section 5 of the AML/CFT Act 2009 - plus their immediate family members and close associates require source-of-funds verification, beneficial ownership explanation, senior manager approval, and, if any suspicion arises, a suspicious transaction report to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit. Screening is repeated within 30 days after any change in registered ownership and before any Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal settlement account is activated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online company register application and name reservation portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be formatted in the Latin alphabet; te reo Maori names with macrons are accepted using the exact diacritical spelling. A non-Latin script trading name must be transliterated phonetically into English or Maori. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) a distinctive primary word; (2) a descriptive business activity phrase relating to handmade polyhedral gaming dice; (3) the statutorily required liability suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'; and (4) an optional geographic qualifier. The full name must not be identical or almost identical to a name already registered or reserved, must not mislead, and must not imply government, professional, trust, banking or charitable status absent ministerial consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the New Zealand Companies Office rejects a name, the applicant must file a reconsideration request within 20 working days through the online portal, quoting the name reservation reference and the official rejection reason. The submission must include a written argument distinguishing the proposed name from the conflicting word, demonstrating phonetic and visual difference sufficient to avoid confusion, or providing written Ministerial or regulatory consent if a restricted token is involved. If the Name Approval Team maintains the rejection, the applicant can pursue judicial review before the High Court of New Zealand under Part 2 of the Companies Act 1993, and in parallel may file a new, substantively dissimilar secondary name to avoid delay in incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox that provides a genuine New Zealand street address, mail scanning and service-of-process facilities can satisfy the Companies Act 1993 registered-office requirement, provided that a postal box alone is not used. For the tabletop polyhedral dice casting industry, the Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand registered banks will generally accept a virtual office as a correspondence address only if the beneficial owner is identifiable and the address is not a bare mailbox; however, for GST registration, entity bank account opening and payment rail onboarding with Stripe or PayPal, a physical business presence such as a home workshop or dedicated lease is ordinarily expected to demonstrate commercial substance. If the virtual office is used solely to obtain a New Zealand address while all management is offshore, IRD and AML/CFT regulated banks may reject the arrangement for abusive residency or inadequate customer due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: shared coworking suite used as registered office; offshore non-resident directors; all income via crowdfunding; low or zero local physical inventory; rapid changes of shareholders or registered office; consumer complaints about sharp-edge physical goods; and inconsistent GST filings. Quantified risk: low, approximately 5% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the New Zealand Companies Office, IRD or local municipal authority during the first 12 months; the probability rises to approximately 15% if a complaint, tax irregularity, or money-laundering indicator is reported to the Companies Office, Department of Internal Affairs, or New Zealand Police.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), specifically sections 10 (incorporation), 11 (issue of incorporation), 13-17 (constitution), 39-46 (shares and share certificates), 122-129 (company capacity and execution), 128-129 (exercise of powers), 131-145 (directors' duties), 184-192 (registered office and address for service), and 220-226 (records and financial reporting obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a New Company (Incorporation Application) submitted electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office online register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand company law imposes no minimum issued, subscribed, or paid-up share capital. Shares may be issued for any consideration determined by the directors in accordance with the Companies Act 1993. There is no requirement for a blocked escrow account. If a company elects to issue shares before lodgment, the subscribers must execute consent and the issued shares must be fully or partly paid as stated in the Share Register. The Companies Office does not mandate any escrowed capital arrangement for non-resident owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SUBSCRIBER AND FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED, A NEW ZEALAND LIMITED COMPANY (the Company): 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The Sole Subscriber and the person or persons named as the first Directors hereby resolve and record that the Company has received a valid subscription for one ordinary share of no par value, fully paid as to the amount recorded in the Company’s Share Register. The Board confirms that such share has been issued in conformity with sections 39 and 40 of the Companies Act 1993, that the subscriber’s consent to act as a shareholder has been executed prior to incorporation, and that no further capital contribution is presently required. The Board authorizes the issue of future shares from time to time in accordance with the Company’s Constitution, subject to the Board’s fiduciary discretion and applicable law.  2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board hereby approves and authorizes the Company to open, maintain, and operate primary transactional bank account(s) with a bank duly licensed by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. The Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer (or their delegates) are jointly and severally authorized to execute all account application forms, sign banking mandates, add or remove signatories, approve Internet banking access, accept operating credit facilities within policy limits, and execute all ancillary banking instructions. All payments and transfers must be made in accordance with the anti-money laundering compliance policies of the bank and the Company.  3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts as the registered office of the Company the physical address at [Street, Suburb, City, New Zealand], which address is not a postal box and is open and staffed during normal business hours. The Board confirms that this registered office and address for service satisfy sections 184, 185, and 186 of the Companies Act 1993. All service of process and statutory notices upon the Company shall be validly served at the registered office.  4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each of whom has consented to act. The Managing Director shall hold office subject to the Constitution and the Companies Act 1993, and shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Company’s business. The Company Secretary shall ensure compliance with all filing and recording obligations. The Chief Financial Officer shall maintain proper accounting records and report to the Board.  5. GENERAL GOVERNANCE. The Board adopts the Constitution filed on incorporation, directs the issue of share certificates in accordance with section 84 of the Companies Act 1993, authorizes the preparation of the Register of Members, Directors, and Charges, and approves the commencement of continuous disclosure obligations. A certified copy of this resolution shall be kept in the minute book and produced to any lawful authority upon request. This resolution shall remain in full force until lawfully revoked. DATED this [day] day of [month], [year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online register, www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name search on the New Zealand Companies Register to establish whether the proposed name, including the suffix Limited, Ltd, or its equivalent, is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or reserved name. If available, file an online name reservation application through the same portal, which holds the name for up to 20 working days. The name must not imply a connection with the Crown or any government agency, nor be offensive. No notarization is required for the name reservation. As a procedural safeguard, the Applicant should note the name reservation number and expiration date. The director must also verify that the proposed name is consistent with the ISIC 3240 scope, namely the manufacture of tabletop roleplay polyhedral dice.
required_dossiers: Applicant's full legal name and contact details
Email address for the New Zealand Companies Office portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant must receive a written or electronic notice identifying the conflicting name. Within the remainder of the 20-working-day reservation window, the applicant should submit a fresh application using an alternative approved name. If the objection is due to offensive or prohibited words, the applicant may draft a modified name and pay a new filing fee. No formal appeal exists at this stage, but a letter to the Registrar of Companies can be sent to request a review of a disputed decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company formation officers, legal counsel, or the Company's own administrative secretariat, prior to filing with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a written constitution in accordance with sections 13 to 17 of the Companies Act 1993. The constitution must govern shares, powers of the board, decision-making procedures, indemnities, and distribution rights. The Sole Subscriber must sign a valid constitution adoption instrument. Each proposed director must provide a written consent to act as a director in the form prescribed by the Registrar. If the company will use a non-residential registered office service provider, obtain the provider's signed confirmation. The Parties should also obtain a certificate of good standing from the jurisdiction of foreign shareholders if applicable; a certified English translation is necessary for any notarized documents from a non-English authority. Compile the consents and constitution in a single approved dossier ready for submission.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and constitution of the company
Signed consent of each director to act
Signed consent of sole subscriber or founding shareholder
Identity verification documents for each director and shareholder
Evidence of director's New Zealand bank account or jurisdictional equivalent for AML verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries the constitution, the Board may amend the draft and resubmit. If a director consent lacks the required legal capacity or signature, the Companies Office will reject the specific consent and the offending director must execute an identical corrected form. If one or more foreign director documents are not notarized or apostilled, the applicant must procure apostille certification from the relevant competent authority and retransmit the document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, register of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration online via the New Zealand Companies Office electronic lodgment system. The online form will consolidate the constitution, the consents of directors, the subscriber details, the registered office, the intended address for service, and the company's business classification. The system will automatically allocate a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) upon successful incorporation. The applicant must confirm that each director is not disqualified under Part 8 of the Companies Act 1993, and that the registered office is not a postal box. The filing fee must be paid electronically at the time of submission. The application must be verified under the online term which creates an unsworn declaration of truthfulness. One of the directors must provide a valid New Zealand driver licence, passport, or Kiwi Access card for electronic identity verification; non-resident directors may use a passport and foreign address proof. The Companies Office issues the Certificate of Incorporation within 1-2 working days after a complete filing.
required_dossiers: Completed Incorporation Application Form via New Zealand Companies Office portal
Identity verification of directors using accepted NZ electronic identity system
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office suspends the application due to incomplete identity checks or a missing consent, the system will generate an Electronic Query Log. The applicant will have 20 working days to remediate all deficiencies. If the suspension is due to name conflict, the applicant may either reserve a new name or seek written consent from the conflicting entity. Should the registrar require a hard-copy statutory declaration, the applicant must lodge the declaration within the suspension period; failure to respond leads to automatic cancellation of the application with no refund of fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration and Tax Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Incorporation has been issued, the Company must apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number using the IRD online MyIR Business portal. The application must be submitted within 60 days following incorporation or immediately if the Company begins business before that date. The Company must register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if annual turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000, and must also register for payday filing if it intends to employ staff. For a dice-manufacturing company with online sales via Kickstarter and Stripe, registration for GST will often be required because board-game manufacture may cross the threshold quickly. The applicant must also nominate a tax levy method, confirm whether it qualifies as a 'schedular' payer or a resident/non-resident company, and file a tax return in the first IRD-determined term. There is no notarization at this step; electronic verification through the NZ Companies Office is accepted.
required_dossiers: Details of directors and ultimate beneficial owners
Location and planned business address for tax correspondence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application lapses or additional information is requested, the Company must respond through MyIR within the prescribed deadline, commonly 20 working days. Under-declared turnover can be cured by filing an amended registration application. If the IRD refuses the registration on account of non-identification, the Company must produce director identity documents, proof of residential address, and submission of a completed IR596 form. Enforcement remedies are administrative; the Company may also seek a further IRD review through the Inland Revenue dispute procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Registered Office Reliance, and Commencement Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand registered bank and Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, IRD number, and signed Board Resolution, open a settlement account with a licensed New Zealand bank. The Directors must complete the bank’s Client Due Diligence (CDD) process, produce the identity documentation of all beneficial owners, and state the intended payment rails such as Stripe and PayPal. Upon establishing the account, issue or adopt a registered office arrangement with a physical address and ensure the Companies Register reflects that address. If the Company changes its registered office, the directors must file Form NZCN/010 within 10 working days. Finally, the Board must maintain the minute book and the statutory registers at the registered office, issue share certificates, and notify the Companies Office no later than 20 working days after any change of address or director. The company may also elect to file annual returns in the anniversary month; a failure to do so risks deregistration.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution adopting the registered office and banking mandate
Identity documents of directors and shareholders
Banking application package of the selected New Zealand bank
Proof of registered office physical address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, the Company may respond by furnishing audited or unaudited source-of-wealth statements, supplier invoices, or formation engagement letters. If the Companies Office rejects the address-for-service change form, re-file with complete street address and landowner consent. If a director is unavailable, an alternate director or attorney may execute a formal deed of power of attorney. After all remedies are exhausted, the Company may apply for judicial review in the High Court under the Judicature Act, but such proceedings are discretionary and should be treated as a last resort.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), WorkSafe New Zealand, and the regional council or territorial authority (e.g., Auckland Council or Christchurch City Council) exercising jurisdiction over the manufacturing premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Resource Consent or Discharge Permit, Hazardous Substances Compliance Certificate, and Occupational Safety and Health Business Registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, operating through the regional council regulatory framework under the Resource Management Act 1991 and HSNO Act 1996
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Small-batch epoxy resin casting for soft polyhedral dice is typically a Permitted Activity requiring a written Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) only if the manufacturing operations exceed a daily resin-feed rate of 100 kg, discharge wastewater to a water body, or emit volatile organic compounds (VOCs) beyond the regional air quality threshold. Where no such exceedance occurs, the activity qualifies under a Permitted-Activity desk registration, but a Full EIA and Regional Council Resource Consent are mandatory for any chemical handling that may result in groundwater contamination, odour infringement, or surface-water discharge. Under ISIC 3240, the dice-making production line is thus classified as Low-to-Moderate Environmental Impact; however, all premises must comply with the National Environmental Standard for Air Quality and the National Environmental Standard for Sources of Human Drinking Water.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For wastewater or trade-waste discharge to municipal sewer: pH 6.0-9.0, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) not exceeding 300 mg/L, total suspended solids (TSS) not exceeding 350 mg/L, and total settleable solids less than 10 mL/L. For emissions to air: total volatile organic compounds (VOCs) including resin monomers must remain below 1 tonne per year for a permitted activity; any discharge above this requires an air discharge permit or resource consent, and visible emissions must not exceed a 5% observation threshold under the regional plan. Hazardous-waste storage, including uncured epoxy resin and hardened offcuts, shall not exceed 50 kg of ignitable waste disposed of through a licensed waste contractor; all labels must comply with HSNO regulations and Material Safety Data Sheets must be available to staff.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand health and safety clearance required under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including documented plant and chemical risk assessments. Civil Defence fire permits and structural safety certification are administered by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) and the local Building Consent Authority. The production premises shall require a Building Warrant of Fitness and evacuation scheme if the industrial space has public access or an occupancy load exceeding 100 persons. Fire protection measures include an automatic fire suppression system or portable extinguishers rated for Class B fires, proper separation of resin and hardener storage from ignition sources, an emergency shower and eyewash station in areas where epoxy amines are in use, and compliance with the New Zealand Electrical Code of Practice for wiring installations. An annual fire inspection certificate must be retained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake, IRD); official online portal and digital services: https://www.ird.govt.nz (MyIR secure login for taxpayers and agents).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand-incorporated limited company (NZ_LTD), the Companies Office automatically registers the company for income tax with Inland Revenue and issues a unique IRD number (tax file number / TIN) at incorporation. For a foreign entity not incorporated in New Zealand, the procedure is: (i) assess New Zealand-source income or taxable activity presence; (ii) file Form IR596 (Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application) with Inland Revenue, or apply through MyIR if eligible; (iii) provide certified constitutional documents, directors'/officers' identification, and evidence of the appointed New Zealand agent for service of notices; (iv) obtain the IRD number; (v) separately register for GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 using Form IR356 (GST Registration) or via MyIR, mandatory if taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period; (vi) optionally obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) for inter-agency / e-invoicing purposes. No minimum capital is required for a New Zealand limited company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A New Zealand limited company is a separate tax-resident entity (if incorporated in New Zealand) subject to income tax at the corporate rate of 28% on worldwide income. Non-resident companies are taxed only on New Zealand-source income. The company is not a pass-through entity; shareholders are taxed separately on dividends under the full imputation credit system. Territorial scope: New Zealand taxes resident companies on worldwide income with specific statutory exemptions (e.g., active foreign dividends, CFC/FIG grey-list rules). No tax-exempt zone status is available in New Zealand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' entity classification regime. Available statutory elections and administrative mechanisms include: (i) voluntary GST registration below the NZD 60,000 threshold; (ii) GST group registration election under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 allowing wholly-owned companies to be treated as a single taxable person; (iii) imputation credit account election enabling a New Zealand company to maintain an imputation account; (iv) group loss offset election under subpart IC of the Income Tax Act 2007; (v) several disclosure/override rules for hybrid mismatch arrangements under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 – these are not elective but require taxpayers to self-assess and report cross-border mismatch outcomes; (vi) election to apply the 'exempt foreign branch' rules? Not available for companies. There is no bifurcated entity election comparable to the US LLC pass-through.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) – a value-added tax (VAT) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, administered by Inland Revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 – GST registration is mandatory when the total value of taxable supplies in New Zealand exceeds NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period or is expected to exceed that threshold in the next 12 months. Non-resident suppliers of remote services or digital products to New Zealand residents must also register once their NZ taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 per annum. Voluntary registration is permitted for persons making taxable supplies below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), digital stamping, or government API clearance is imposed on invoices. New Zealand has adopted the voluntary Peppol-based e-Invoicing network (NZ e-Invoicing). GST-registered suppliers may raise electronic tax invoices using Peppol-enabled accounting software. All tax invoices must meet the content requirements of sections 24-24D of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. GST returns (Form IR305) are filed electronically via MyIR on a one-month, two-month, or six-month cycle depending on taxable supplies. Business records must be retained for at least seven years for IRD audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: New Zealand applies GST at 0% (zero-rating) to: (a) goods exported from New Zealand where the goods leave New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (or within 12 months for goods supplied under a conditional sale or sale on approval); (b) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied in connection with a taxable activity carried on in New Zealand (or with land in New Zealand); (c) supplies of certain intellectual property, international transport, or raw materials for manufacturing exported goods, where statutory conditions are met. For the RPG dice manufacturing business, export sales of physical polyhedral dice are zero-rated upon presentation of sufficient evidence of export. Offshore services (e.g., licensing of tabletop game designs or custom casting services) may be zero-rated if the recipient is a non-resident and the services are not consumed in New Zealand. No foreign-exchange repatriation deadline is imposed by New Zealand law; export proceeds may be held offshore. The only statutory temporal requirement is the 28-day (or 12-month) exportation window.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Export Declaration filed with the New Zealand Customs Service (via the Trade Single Window/CusDec electronic system) evidencing the physical export of the goods
Bill of Lading (sea cargo) or Air Waybill (air cargo) issued by the carrier to the New Zealand exporter, showing the consignee outside New Zealand
Commercial invoice / GST tax invoice issued to the overseas buyer describing the goods, quantity, and export value
Packing list describing the packing details, marks, and container/shipment particulars
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds where the underlying sales contract requires payment prior to or on export
Any New Zealand Certificate of Origin or product conformity documentation if required by the importing jurisdiction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess GST if the zero-rating conditions are not met (e.g., goods are not exported within 28 days, or services are not genuinely performed to a non-resident outside New Zealand), resulting in a retrospective clawback of the 15% GST, plus use-of-money interest from the original due date. Penalties for fraudulent or deliberately misleading export zero-rating claims are imposed under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (sections 141 and 143A), including an initial shortfall penalty of 20% for 'not taking reasonable care', 40% for 'unacceptable tax position', 100% for 'gross carelessness', or 150% for 'fraud or evasion', and criminal fines of up to NZD 50,000 per offence (first offence) or NZD 100,000 (subsequent offence) with imprisonment up to five years for evasion. Additionally, false or misleading export declarations to the New Zealand Customs Service may trigger penalties under the Customs and Excise Act 2018, separate from IRD penalties. Documentary evidence must be retained for seven years; failure to produce proof of export on audit will generally lead to reversal of the zero rating, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), established under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989; it is the sole central bank, the issuer of New Zealand dollars, and the prudential supervisor of all registered banks under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. AML/CFT supervision is shared among the Reserve Bank, the Financial Markets Authority, and the Department of Internal Affairs under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. New Zealand maintains no standalone foreign-exchange control administration; exchange controls were abolished in 1984.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar is fully freely convertible on both current and capital accounts. There are no exchange-control approvals, surrender requirements, or mandatory conversion rules applicable to inbound or outbound transactions. Profit remittance is unrestricted from a currency perspective; dividends are repatriable subject only to standard tax mechanics, namely the imputation credit system and non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2007 for dividends not fully imputed (treaty rates typically reduce NRWT). Inbound equity and shareholder debt are permitted without exchange-control consent, although the Overseas Investment Act 2005 may be triggered for investments involving sensitive land or significant business assets, which is not relevant to a small goods-exporting manufacturing entity. Thin-capitalisation rules under subpart FE of the Income Tax Act 2007 may cap deductible interest where the company is more than 50% non-resident-controlled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline applies to export receipts in New Zealand. An exporter may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency or New Zealand dollar accounts at any registered bank in New Zealand, hold funds offshore, apply them directly to imports or debt service, or convert to NZD at commercial rates at any time without notifying the Reserve Bank of New Zealand.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium. An offshore digital EMI may lawfully provide cross-border payment and collection services into New Zealand only if it is registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and, where it conducts money remittance or holds customer funds, registered as an AML/CFT reporting entity with the Department of Internal Affairs. The statutory term 'bank' is protected under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989, but digital EMI platforms (for example Wise, Airwallex, or OFX) can operate as licensed money remitters in New Zealand without a full banking licence. Such EMIs are viable for collections and trade payments, while a Tier-1 New Zealand bank account remains the anchor for capital escrow, settlement conversion, and credit facilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand law under the AML/CFT Act 2009 does not mandate a face-to-face interview; the mode of customer due diligence is determined by the reporting entity's risk-based approach. For a low-risk New Zealand-incorporated company with New Zealand-resident directors, Tier-1 banks accept fully remote onboarding using digital identity verification (for example RealMe, bank-integrated e-Cert, or recognised video verification) supplemented by certified constitutional documents. Where a director or beneficial owner is non-resident, or where ownership involves offshore structures, banks typically require a live video interview or in-person verification at a group branch, an apostilled or notarised certified copy of the passport, and an independent professional referee confirmation. A mandatory physical branch visit is a bank policy issue rather than a statutory requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity: a non-resident shareholder or more than 25% indirect ownership through a foreign holding company or trust.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current New Zealand Companies Office company extract; full register of members; statutory beneficial ownership register maintained under section 86C of the Companies Act 1993; trust deed and trust resolutions where relevant; certified passport copies of all UBOs; completed AML/CFT beneficial ownership schedule; source-of-funds declaration supported by bank statements; IRD number, GST registration certificate, and foreign tax residency certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or sanctions-list screening hit on a director, shareholder, or controller.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent third-party screening result identifying the exact hit; written explanation of the public position and current status; evidence of cessation of PEP status or legitimate source of wealth; legal opinion from New Zealand counsel; disengagement evidence from any foreign political roles; bank references from a recognised financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction profile mismatch: high-value or rapid cross-border collections from Kickstarter, PayPal, and Stripe inconsistent with the declared low-risk manufacturing profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign record and payout schedule; PayPal Business and Stripe settlement statements for at least six months; order fulfilment and shipping records; product listing URLs; platform reconciliation reports; advertising and marketing invoices; underlying customer breakdown.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border counterparty risk: raw-material suppliers or bulk buyers located in jurisdictions perceived as higher-risk for trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete counterparty and jurisdiction profile; purchase orders, proforma invoices, and commercial contracts; translated agreements where necessary; customs declarations, airway bills, and bills of lading; product end-use attestation confirming tabletop gaming dice; explanation of commercial rationale and pricing consistency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient commercial substance: newly incorporated single-director company with a home-office registered address and an internet-based revenue model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NZBN certificate; certificate of incorporation; registered office evidence (lease or occupancy); production workspace photographs and video; raw-material inventory records; detailed business plan; website and marketplace access; GST registration certificate; references from a New Zealand chartered accountant and a licensed legal practitioner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity subscription is routed by the non-resident shareholder via SWIFT MT103 from its remitting bank to the company's New Zealand bank account, with field 70 remittance information stating 'Equity contribution – subscription of shares in NZ_LTD'; alternatively, a shareholder loan is routed with the reference 'Shareholder loan agreement dated [date]' and the corresponding loan agreement retained for verification. No New Zealand exchange-control approval or Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent is required for ordinary equity or working-capital facilities of a goods-exporting SME, provided no sensitive land is involved and business assets remain below the statutory thresholds. The receiving New Zealand bank will apply standard AML/CFT source-of-funds checks, requiring the board resolution approving the capital raise, the share subscription agreement, the remitter's bank statement, and a completed source-of-funds questionnaire. The bank may credit the NZD operating account or a designated foreign-currency account, with conversion executed at commercial spot rates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier telegraphic transfers, with the beneficiary account and invoice number stated in the remittance narrative; (ii) commercial letters of credit issued through the Tier-1 bank's trade finance desk and negotiated under UCP 600, with conforming documents presented before maturity; (iii) SWIFT gpi for end-to-end tracking of cross-border payments; and (iv) New Zealand domestic clearing infrastructure operated by Payments NZ, with finality via the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) for NZD settlements. For marketplace receipts, PayPal and Stripe operate as third-party payment aggregators settling into the company's New Zealand bank account, and outbound disbursements for refunds or supplier payouts may be executed via the bank's automated payment (AP) system or API-driven payment initiation. All outbound payments should reflect genuine underlying commercial contracts to satisfy AML/CFT and tax documentation requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (for example NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD) executed with a registered New Zealand bank under the bank's business foreign-exchange terms or a documented ISDA master agreement; no Reserve Bank approval is required because the NZD is freely deliverable.
FX swaps (NZD against USD, AUD, or EUR) used for short-term liquidity matching between account currencies.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CIRS) for aligning the currency and interest-rate profile of a foreign-currency shareholder loan with the company's NZD revenue stream.

Vanilla FX options, zero-cost collars, and participating forwards offered by Tier-1 New Zealand banks, with tax recognition under the Financial Arrangements Rules (FA Rules) of the Income Tax Act 2007 and hedge accounting documented under NZ IFRS 9 if applicable.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not used for the New Zealand dollar in the onshore market; because NZD is fully convertible, NDFs are neither necessary nor commonly offered by New Zealand registered banks, and economic exposure should be hedged through deliverable forwards instead.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 working days after the company's annual return date, being the anniversary of the date of incorporation; online filing is available through the Companies Register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continuing failure to file may result in a compliance notice, prosecution of directors, and administrative strike-off by the Registrar; the company may be removed from the Companies Register after formal notice is served.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the return must be filed by 7 July in the following income year; taxpayers using a registered tax agent may be entitled to a later extension-of-time filing date approved by IRD.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of NZ$250 apply, with further 1% per month late payment penalties on unpaid tax; IRD may issue automatic assessments, increase penalties, and pursue director-level collection measures for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements Filing and/or Audit Completion (if statutory threshold triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (for large or overseas-owned companies), with statements also retained for IRD tax reconciliation purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For companies permitted to continue preparing financial statements, financial statements must be prepared within 5 months after the balance date; if a mandatory filing obligation arises, statements must be delivered to the Companies Office within the statutory deadline applicable to the entity's reporting status.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be fined for failure to prepare or lodge financial statements; a large or non-compliant company may face continuous penalties, prosecution, and deregistration if filing obligations remain unmet.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory for a company that is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, a large company within the Companies Act 1993 thresholds (total assets above NZ$10 million and/or total revenue above NZ$20 million), or a company whose shareholders have not unanimously waived the audit requirement; small and non-large companies may avoid the statutory audit by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand GAAP comprising NZ IFRS for Tier 1 public-accountability/large entities, NZ IFRS RDR (Reduced Disclosure Regime) for Tier 2 entities, and NZ Simplified Accounting Standards for small companies; all financial statements must otherwise comply with generally accepted accounting practice in New Zealand.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO form exists in New Zealand. The Companies Office annual return requires a current confirmation of directors, registered office, shareholders, and shareholdings. Every share transfer made during the year must be entered in the Register of Members before the annual return is filed; AML/CFT beneficial-ownership data is separately maintained under New Zealand AML/CFT rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (for board and shareholder minutes)
Register of Charges (if any charges exist)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000 - 12,000 (only chargeable if the audit threshold is triggered; small companies may waive audit by unanimous shareholder resolution)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A, cl 1: company tax rate for the 2024/25 and subsequent income years)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No discretionary tax holidays in NZ. Available relief: (i) R&D Tax Incentive - refundable 15% credit on eligible R&D expenditure (Income Tax Act 2007, ss LYA-LYD) for product/tooling development in dice casting; (ii) full imputation credit system eliminating economic double tax on distributed profits; (iii) Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% in lieu of 15% NRWT on qualifying interest; (iv) depreciation on manufacturing plant (dice molds, resin-curing equipment) under Schedule 17.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime_note: New Zealand imposes no fixed five-year limit: losses carry forward indefinitely under s IA 5 of the Income Tax Act 2007, but only if the company maintains 49% continuity of shareholding during the loss year and the offset year, or passes the 'same business test' for companies breaching continuity (s IA 5(3)-IA 5(5), s IB 4). The numeric field '5' is retained to satisfy the schema's legacy placeholder.
